content.value_statement: Competitor ads reveal market positioning, pain points, and creative patterns. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code turn public ad libraries into campaign insights.
actual_capabilities: Guides extraction of competitor ads from public ad libraries.
Organizes ad screenshots and source material for review.
Analyzes messages, pain points, value propositions, and calls to action.
Groups ads by theme, audience, format, and creative pattern.
Compares multiple competitors to identify common and different positioning.
Produces reports, spreadsheets, decks, or pattern libraries from the research.
limitations: Results depend on public ad library access and platform availability.
Engagement and performance data may be unavailable or incomplete.
The skill provides marketing research, not legal or compliance advice.
Users must create original ads and avoid copying competitor creative.

use_cases.title: Plan New Campaign Angles
use_cases.description: Review competitor ads to find repeated pain points, offer themes, and creative formats before building test campaigns.

use_cases.title: Map Market Positioning
use_cases.description: Compare several competitors to understand category messages, audience segments, and underserved claims.

use_cases.title: Build Creative References
use_cases.description: Save public ad examples, group them by pattern, and brief designers with original concepts based on research.

prompt_templates.title: Extract One Competitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract current public ads for [Competitor] from Facebook Ad Library. Summarize the main messages, offers, formats, and calls to action.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Message Theme
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused analysis of a specific pain point.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [Competitor] ads that mention [pain point]. Identify the copy patterns, proof points, audience signals, and creative approaches.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Competitive Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract ads from [Company A], [Company B], and [Company C]. Compare themes, positioning, offers, visual formats, and gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Track Message Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [Competitor] ads from [period one] and [period two]. Explain what changed, what stayed consistent, and what tests we should run.

output_examples.input: Extract current Facebook ads for a project management competitor.
output: Primary themes include collaboration, task visibility, and fewer meetings.
Most calls to action use free trial language and short benefit statements.
Recommended tests include problem-first headlines and product screenshot creatives.

output_examples.input: Compare three competitors in the same category.
output: Company A leads with speed, Company B leads with control, and Company C leads with simplicity.
All three use customer proof, but only one highlights migration support.
The clearest gap is messaging for finance teams and compliance buyers.

output_examples.input: Analyze video ads versus static image ads for one competitor.
output: Video ads explain workflow steps, while static ads focus on one clear outcome.
Static ads use shorter copy and stronger calls to action.
A useful test is a short product demo video against a single-benefit image ad.

best_practices: Use only public ad library data and follow each platform policy.
Look for repeated patterns instead of treating one ad as proof.
Use insights to create original campaigns, copy, and visuals.
anti_patterns: Do not copy competitor ads, designs, screenshots, or claims directly.
Do not assume an active ad is a winning ad without supporting evidence.
Do not scrape private, gated, or unauthorized sources.

faq.question: What platforms can this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It is written for public ad libraries such as Facebook Ad Library and LinkedIn ads where access is available.

faq.question: Does it know which ads perform best?
faq.answer: It can infer likely patterns from frequency and messaging, but direct performance data may not be available.

faq.question: Can I use the competitor copy in my own ads?
faq.answer: No. Use the analysis for research and inspiration, then write original copy and create original visuals.

faq.question: Can it compare several competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes workflows for comparing themes, positioning, formats, and gaps across multiple competitors.

faq.question: What outputs can it produce?
faq.answer: It can produce a written analysis, screenshot library, spreadsheet, presentation outline, or categorized pattern library.

faq.question: Is this a compliance tool?
faq.answer: No. It supports marketing research. Users remain responsible for platform rules, intellectual property, and legal review.
